title.narrative: Activity under preparation Breaking Barriers; Building Futures: Enhancing Economic and Social Inclusion of Women and Girls in Uganda

description.narrative: This Action ¿Breaking Barriers, Building Futures: Enhancing Economic and Social Inclusion of Women and Girls in Uganda¿ aims at empowering women in Uganda (including in refugee communities) by improving their economic and social inclusion. The overall objective of this action is to contribute to harnessing the demographic dividend and to reducing vulnerabilities and gender inequality among young people, including refugees, in Uganda. The proposed action aims to empower women and girls by improving their economic wellbeing, reducing sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), and increasing access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services. This will enable them to participate fully in economic activities, make informed choices about their reproductive health, and live in a safer environment, ultimately enhancing their economic, social, and physical wellbeing. The action will target vulnerable areas, including refugee-hosting districts, to operationalise the triple nexus in line with the Comprehensive Refugee Response Framework (CRRF). By strengthening livelihoods, health, and SGBV protection, this programme supports both refugees and host communities, reinforcing Uganda¿s stability and development. This action is part of the Team Europe Initiative for Social Inclusion, complementing the ongoing Gender for Development Uganda (G4DU) programme that addresses financial and societal barriers to girls¿ transition from primary to secondary education, as well as other EU and EU Member States -financed programmes (We Care ¿ Belgium, SAY ¿ Denmark, HEROES for transformative action ¿ Netherlands) contributing to the TEI. It will particularly help advancing the TEI results 1 (Access to SRHR and family planning), 2 (SGBV prevention and response) and 3 (Education for adolescent girls). The overall indicative budget for the TEI for the period 2022-2027 is over EUR 914 million with funding from the EU, Austria, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands and Sweden. Since 2022, Team Europe members have committed some EUR 238 million of new funding for the implementation of the TEI.The TEI has already achieved important results since its inception in 2022 in the focus areas of this action, including: 3.9 million women supported with maternal health care, over 24 million individuals informed on how to prevent Sexual Gender Based Violence, over 1 million adolescents supported to complete primary and to transition to lower secondary, thanks to TEI support.
